slot.brief: A car negotiates a banked curve with friction; find the range of safe speeds or maximum speed using tanθ-based formula.

stem: A car negotiates a circular turn of radius $10\ \text{m}$ on a road banked at an angle of $45^\circ$. If the coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the road is $0.6$, the maximum safe speed of the car to avoid skidding outward is (take $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$):

verdicts.working: For maximum speed on a banked road with friction acting down the incline: v_max = sqrt(rg(tanθ+μ)/(1−μtanθ)) = sqrt(10·10·(1+0.6)/(1−0.6)) = sqrt(400) = 20 m/s.

working:
The maximum safe speed $v_{\max}$ on a banked road with friction is given by the formula:
$$v_{\max} = \sqrt{R g \left(\dfrac{\tan\theta + \mu}{1 - \mu \tan\theta}\right)}$$

Given data:
- $R = 10\ \text{m}$
- $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$
- $\theta = 45^\circ \implies \tan 45^\circ = 1$
- $\mu = 0.6$

Substitute the values into the formula:
$$\dfrac{\tan\theta + \mu}{1 - \mu \tan\theta} = \dfrac{1 + 0.6}{1 - 0.6 \times 1} = \dfrac{1.6}{0.4} = 4$$

$$v_{\max} = \sqrt{10 \times 10 \times 4} = \sqrt{400} = 20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$$

Independent check: For maximum speed on a banked road with friction acting down the incline: v_max = sqrt(rg(tanθ+μ)/(1−μtanθ)) = sqrt(10·10·(1+0.6)/(1−0.6)) = sqrt(400) = 20 m/s.

draft.distractor_notes:
$5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$: Minimum safe speed below which the car slides down the bank, $v_{\min} = \sqrt{Rg\frac{\tan\theta - \mu}{1 + \mu\tan\theta}} = \sqrt{100 \times 0.25} = 5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
$10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$: Optimum banking speed ignoring friction, $v_0 = \sqrt{Rg\tan\theta} = \sqrt{100 \times 1} = 10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
$15\ \text{m s}^{-1}$: Arithmetic mean of the minimum and maximum safe speeds, $\frac{v_{\min} + v_{\max}}{2} = \frac{5 + 20}{2} = 12.5 \approx 15$, or $(v_0 + v_{\max})/2 = 15\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
